findings.pdf_says:
c) If the TEST AFTER phrase is specified, and there is one or more AFTER phrase, the following occurs:
    1. The specified set of statements is executed.
    2. The rightmost condition-2 is then evaluated.
    3. If the rightmost condition-2 is false, ... and execution proceeds with step a.
    4. If the last condition evaluated is true, ...
        NOTE After successful execution of the PERFORM statement, all induction variables contain the values they had at the completion of the last execution of the specified set of statements.
findings.markdown_says:
c) If the TEST AFTER phrase is specified, and there is one or more AFTER phrase, the following occurs:

   1\. The specified set of statements is executed.

   2\. The rightmost condition-2 is then evaluated.

   3\. If the rightmost condition-2 is false, the associated induction variable is incremented by the associated augment value, and execution proceeds with step a.

   4\. If the last condition evaluated is true, ...

   NOTE After successful execution of the PERFORM statement, all induction variables contain the values they had at the completion of the last execution of the specified set of statements.
findings.why_it_matters: The numbered steps 1-4 (and the NOTE under step 4) are printed as sub-items of PERFORM general rule 9 c), indented one level deeper; the transcription places them at the same indentation as items a)-e), so they read as siblings of c) rather than its body, and the trailing NOTE reads as applying to the whole of rule 9.
findings.note: Wording is exact; only the list nesting is lost. The same flattening continues onto page 572 (p572-1).

findings.pdf_says:
1. Condition-1 is evaluated. ... 2. The current condition is evaluated.
        If the current condition is true:
            a. the induction variable associated with the current condition is set to its initialization value
            b. the condition to the left of the current condition becomes the current condition ...
        otherwise:
            a. if there is another AFTER phrase to the right of the current condition,
                —the condition associated with that AFTER phrase becomes the current condition
                —execution proceeds to the beginning of step b;
            b. otherwise
                —the specified set of statements is executed ...
findings.markdown_says:
1\. Condition-1 is evaluated.

   If condition-1 is true, ...

   2\. The current condition is evaluated.

   If the current condition is true:

   a. the induction variable associated with the current condition is set to its initialization value

   b. the condition to the left of the current condition becomes the current condition
...
   otherwise:

   a. if there is another AFTER phrase to the right of the current condition,

   —the condition associated with that AFTER phrase becomes the current condition

   —execution proceeds to the beginning of step b;

   b. otherwise

   —the specified set of statements is executed
findings.why_it_matters: PERFORM general rule 9 e) is a four-level nested algorithm (numbered steps 1-2 under e), lettered a.-d. under 'If the current condition is true:' and a.-b. under 'otherwise:', em-dash actions under each). The transcription flattens every level to one indentation, so the two separate a./b. lists, the em-dash actions, and the e) parent are indistinguishable, and the cross-references 'step a' / 'step b' become ambiguous between the a)/b) rules, the 'true' a./b. and the 'otherwise' a./b. This is the normative execution order of PERFORM VARYING ... AFTER with TEST BEFORE.
findings.note: Wording is exact; only the list nesting is lost. Continues the flattening from p571-1 (rule 9 e) begins at the foot of page 571).
